text:
Ryker Evans has become a 22-minute defenseman in Seattle, and he is holding up. He has eight points in 20 games, and Seattle is about four points better on five-on-five expected goals with him on than without (expected goals measure the quality of chances), on a team that is badly under water overall.

His three goals are a bonus he shouldn't count on: they come on less than one expected goal, and the team has scored about 4.4 more goals than its chances with him out there. Evolving-Hockey had him 56th among 215 defensemen last season, mostly from even-strength offense, while Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his game isn't built on creating at five on five. He carries the puck in on 42% of his entries and plays a physical game, 32 hits and 32 blocks. A second-round pick by the Kraken in 2021 out of Regina, he is 24. Our range has him around 30 points.
